title: The Farmer and the King
summary: A poor farmer offers Akbar a basket of wild plums, while a wealthy prince offers jewels. Birbal reveals which gift was truly greater.
full_text:
On Emperor Akbar's fortieth birthday, princes, nawabs, and wealthy merchants from across Hindustan arrived at the Agra Fort, presenting magnificent tributes: chests of uncut diamonds, gold-embroidered tapestries, thoroughbred Arabian horses, and ivory statues.

At the very end of the long procession of dignitaries stood a poor, sun-browned farmer named Govind from a distant village. In his trembling hands, he carried a small, woven cane basket containing twenty wild, tart plums picked from his small orchard.

The courtiers sneered: 'Look at that peasant! Bringing sour roadside plums to the Emperor on his birthday! He should be driven out!'

Govind knelt humbly, placing his basket at the foot of the throne: 'Your Majesty, I am a poor man. I have no gold or pearls. But these plums are the sweetest first fruits of my trees, harvested with love for my sovereign.'

Akbar took a plum, tasted it, smiled, and placed the basket on his royal table beside the diamond chests.

Later, in private council, a nobleman remarked: 'Sire, why did you honor that peasant's worthless plums alongside chests of emeralds?'

Birbal spoke with deep conviction:

'My lord, consider the proportion of the gifts. The wealthy nawabs gave you two chests of rubies from treasuries that hold ten thousand chests. Their gift cost them nothing; they will not miss a single coin, nor will their children ever go hungry.

'But this poor farmer has only two plum trees to feed his family. By giving you twenty plums, he gave you the food of his children and the labor of his hands. He gave away half of everything he possessed in the world!

'A gift is great not because of its price in the market, but because of the sacrifice it represents in the heart of the giver.'

Akbar agreed wholeheartedly, and ordered a pair of sturdy bullocks, a bag of seed grain, and fertile land gifted to the honest farmer.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Farmer and the King"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
